data.one_liner: Async SQLite access on the web via workers with automatic storage detection
data.what_it_does: Provides a Dart API to run SQLite in web workers, handling async communication, feature detection, and storage backend selection. It exposes a WebSqlite class that opens databases, runs queries, and manages locks.
use_when: You need SQLite on the web and prefer async worker-based access
You want automatic detection of the best persistence API (IndexedDB, OPFS, etc.)
You are building a higher-level library that requires a worker‑based SQLite backend
avoid_when: You are building a simple web app that can use localStorage or IndexedDB directly
You need a pure synchronous API
strengths: Worker‑based async access avoids blocking the UI
Automatic detection of available storage backends
Built for integration with higher‑level libraries like sqlite_async or drift
weaknesses: Requires a wasm binary and worker setup
Setup can be complex for beginners
No direct support for non‑web platforms
data.setup_notes: Add sqlite3.wasm to your web assets, compile worker with dart compile js, and provide WorkerConnector to WebSqlite.open
